Can you provide short-term access to Redwood's Trust Portal so our internal security team and external auditor can complete a targeted review? Timing: our audit kickoff is Friday 11/05 and we'd like a 48-hour window that starts no earlier than Thursday 11/04. If possible, include a bridge letter that covers the period after the report up to the audit kickoff.

Contacts: Kyle Hart (security@aperturehealth.com) and our auditor Northbridge Audit (susan.liu@northbridgeaudit.com).

Any compliance or NDAs you need us to sign first, let us know — happy to get those in place.

Kyle — thanks for the note and the clear ask. We can accommodate a timeboxed, viewer-only session and we can produce a redacted extract focused on encryption and retention controls. A few clarifying items before I provision access:

- Who will actually perform the review (internal names + emails)? Please list the auditors by name — we need to map SSO invite to specific identities.
- Is the preference for an Okta one-time SSO link or a Trust Portal guest account? We typically recommend the one-time SSO for shortest blast radius.
- Are you expecting downloads of evidence artifacts (e.g., logs, screenshots), or will viewing in the portal suffice? We can allow limited downloads if required.

Proposed default: 48-hour one-time SSO viewer window starting 2027-11-04 08:00 PT. We'll attach a draft bridge letter for your review. If you need an extended window, note that any extension will need approval from our compliance team.

I'm looping Marissa (Security) and Karthik (Trust) to draft the bridge letter and prepare the extract.

If that works, send me the final auditor list and I'll start the provisioning.

- Logan

Logan Wright
Partner Success — Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — quick internal note and proposed approach: 

1) Access pattern: issue a one-time SSO (ephemeral) link scoped to 'viewer' for the specified auditor identities. Link will be timeboxed and IP-restricted to the auditor's VPN ranges where provided.
2) Downloads: allow attachments folder downloads only (evidence artifacts) for named auditor accounts; disable copy-paste on report viewer.
3) Report extract: compliance will produce a redacted PDF that includes control narratives, testing procedures, and test outcomes for controls related to encryption (data-at-rest, data-in-transit) and retention. No raw log exports.
4) Bridge letter: draft attached — covers the period 2027-07-01 through report issuance and includes a short statement about no material design changes to the covered controls.

Window: recommend 72 hours to give auditors some scheduling flexibility. If Aperture insists on 48, escalate. If they need >72 then security review required (we may require a temporary NDA addendum).

I'll prepare the evidence index CSV and mark sensitive artifacts for view-only. Karthik, can you prep the portal scope and generate the ephemeral link once I confirm the final auditor list?

Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference
